title: Launch Corridor: Capacity Hedging & Stakeholder Runway for Runtime/Console/API
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Goal: Define and operationalize a 'launch corridor' playbook that hedges capacity for critical runtime/console/API rollouts, preserves stakeholder runway, and codifies traffic-shaping and fallback signals. This ticket synthesizes capacity simulation outputs, stakeholder commitments, canary cohort sizing, and cutover/runbook ownership so launches hit SLOs while minimizing cross-surface blast radius.

Scope: strategy + runbook for coordinated launches affecting the runtime API, Console release windows, and model rollout switchovers. Not implementing autoscaling algorithms (ENG work) but defining guardrails, acceptance criteria, and interlock signals for shipping teams.

Intended outcomes: clear capacity escrow guidelines per priority lane, a standard stakeholder runway matrix, signal thresholds for abort/rollback/fail-open, and a lightweight playbook for preflight smoke and shadow runs.

Key artifacts: Confluence spec, capacity simulator dashboards, runbook template, and a sample rollout sequence for a high-risk model quantization change.
milestones: Draft playbook and capacity hedging matrix (2025-02-24)
Finalize runbook and publish training doc (2025-03-28)
acceptance_criteria: Published 'launch corridor' playbook in Confluence with owner and escalation map
Capacity hedging matrix defines minimum reserved GPU/vCPU by priority lane and region
Stakeholders (Runtime, Console, API, SRE, Product) have signed the runway commitments
Canary cohort sizing guidance with traffic percent buckets and detection thresholds
Preflight smoke checklist and two-step shadow run protocol documented
Dashboards with the three primary launch signals (latency p95, error rate, token cost delta) configured and linked in runbook
risks: Under-reserving capacity for cross-region spikes leading to SLO violations
Stakeholder overcommitment: launches without honoring reserved lanes
Insufficient observability for sudden model regressions during canaries
Operational complexity increases time-to-launch for small, low-risk fixes
mitigations: Create a lightweight capacity escrow pool that can be reclaimed with 24h notice
Automated preflight checks gate launch: shadow run + perf regressions must pass
Runbook includes automatic fallback routing to a cost-optimized compatible model variant
Provide a 'fastlane' checklist for low-risk micro releases that don't require full corridor reservation
